claims.passage: Giving more antiemetic agents than the risk score indicated was associated with sedation that delayed discharge in 6 percent of patients, compared with 2 percent of patients whose prophylaxis matched the score.

synthesis: Six retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Adherence to risk-tailored prophylaxis was about half in one large study, with high-risk patients under-treated most often. A case-control analysis found under-prophylaxis associated with rescue treatment, and a recovery nausea log captured most rescue treatments, which makes rescue treatment a workable case definition. Over-prophylaxis was associated with sedation delaying discharge rather than fewer rescue treatments. Nausea caused about a third of unplanned admissions in three units. The evidence supports a local case-control study with record reading, with separate attention to over-prophylaxis.
gradeRationale: Observational studies with confounding by indication and unblinded record reading; consistent in direction.
summary: Six records appraised; four claims; certainty low.
